label: Physical description
value: A thick rectangular **slab computer** about the footprint of a small 13–14″ laptop but thicker and denser. Matte charcoal/black polymer or powder-coated aluminum shell. No glossy consumer laptop lid logo. One short edge has a dense **port cluster**: USB-C, USB-A, Ethernet-style RJ45, small HDMI, and a row of exposed GPIO-style pins under a rubber dust flap. Opposite short edge has a **sling/D-ring** and a recessed power button. Top face is mostly flat with a dark matte display bezel (display may be closed/covered in field shots). Bottom has shallow rubber feet and a battery door seam. Optional muted institutional stripe (ivory, 4 mm) along one long edge only — no bright RGB.

label: Core concept
value: Apex Tactical Corp is the de facto organization behind McCluster Corp and several other front corporations. It uses those entities to operate black sites, manage sensitive work and deal with governments throughout the world.

label: Structure
value:
Apex does not need to resemble a conventional public holding company. Control may be distributed through contracts, ownership vehicles, classified authorities, technical access and personnel loyalty.

Its fronts compartmentalize:

- Public business
- Recruitment
- Government relationships
- Research and development
- Logistics
- Field operations
- Black-site infrastructure
- Liability and attribution

Only McCluster Corp is currently named and canonized. Do not invent additional front corporations without owner approval.

label: Prime relationship
value:
Prime is Apex's highest operational authority.

The Prime office has access and responsibilities beyond any ordinary executive position. The exact legal relationship between Prime, Apex ownership and individual front corporations remains intentionally opaque until later story development.

label: Narrative purpose
value:
McCluster Corp lets the protagonist believe he has joined an exceptional company.

Apex Tactical Corp is the first revelation that he has joined an architecture.

Prime is the later revelation that the architecture belongs operationally to one person who cannot resign.

label: Role
value: Day-to-day workplace, training campus and recurring ensemble home.

label: Culture rule
value: Functional mirror to PRIM, with different culture and operational identity.

label: Story function
value:
McCluster Corp is the apparently legitimate corporation that hires the protagonist during his first year of college. It is the audience's public entrance into the hidden Prime system.

McCluster Corp is a front owned and controlled by Apex Tactical Corp.

label: Public face
value:
McCluster Corp presents as a prestigious, culturally sophisticated technology corporation. Its recruiting materials, facilities, employees and clothing communicate opportunity, intelligence, taste and institutional power.

The company can perform real work and employ people who never discover its full purpose. A front is more durable when its public layer genuinely functions.

label: Hidden function
value:
McCluster Corp provides Apex Tactical Corp with:

- A legitimate recruiting pipeline
- Employment and academic-internship cover
- Access to technical talent
- Contract administration
- Data and candidate evaluation
- A clean corporate identity between governments and classified Apex operations
- A place to observe candidates before exposing them to the real organization

label: Season one
value:
The protagonist is formally hired by McCluster Corp, not Apex Tactical Corp.

During onboarding, he receives high-level designer corporate swag built from the exact McCluster Dual Sight monogram. Everyone inside the corporation wears branded clothing or accessories.

Because he enters from homelessness and severe financial instability, the clothing carries emotional weight. It is one of the first visible signs that an institution considers him valuable.

The brand is part of the seduction.

label: Knowledge boundaries
value:
- Ordinary employees may believe McCluster Corp is independent.
- Selected staff may know that a parent or government-contract layer exists without knowing Apex's scale.
- Cohort candidates gradually discover that McCluster Corp's hierarchy, permissions and mission exposure cannot be explained by its public business.
- The public does not automatically know that Apex Tactical Corp owns or controls McCluster Corp.

label: Design intent
value: Demonstrate that wireless concepts become tactical map state: Field-R maps signal and confidence, Field-E physically creates a safe relay position under weather/contact, and Field-T restores authenticated usable service. Shooting can buy time but can also damage power/backhaul and worsen the communications problem.

value.description: Restore one authenticated, usable responder communications path.
Establish and hold a physically safe relay/backhaul position long enough to validate service.
value.completion_predicate: relay_zone_control == SECURE and relay_power in [NORMAL, BACKUP_STABLE]

value.description: Preserve limited public check-in connectivity without stealing responder capacity.
Preserve enough spectrum/service telemetry to explain the failure after the incident.
Do not send operators into electrically or structurally unsafe areas merely to chase signal strength.

value.evidence_predicate: R maps at least one strong-signal zone and one low-signal/dead zone accurately
R identifies the unapproved source using inventory plus observed characteristics rather than signal strength alone
R marks unknown source as likely/suspect until independent evidence confirms it
player recognizes that physical RF/power/backhaul conditions can fail before higher-layer service is considered
player distinguishes radio presence from local link/service state in the abstracted dashboard
T selects the approved authenticated service profile rather than open/unknown shortcut
player understands encryption is one property of the trusted service and not proof that source/backhaul/power is correct
E selects a safe relay position and manually stabilizes power/physical access before T commits configuration
suspicious wireless source is identified/isolated through defensive monitoring and authorized response
player restores usable service by treating AP, power, backhaul, authentication, and coverage as separate dependencies

value: A player can see strong signal and still fail service verification.

label: Design intent
value: First end-to-end PRIM3 vertical slice proving that a song's IT concepts can be learned through the same six-AP tactical economy as movement, cover, shooting, suppression, reconnaissance, physical control, and extraction.

value.description: Contain the affected personnel/training service without destroying the evidence needed to understand the incident.
Establish a defensible impact scope from correlated evidence rather than assumption.
Preserve high-value logs and McCluster's pre-recruitment dossier without response-driven privacy leakage.
Keep the minimum trusted training/notification functions available during containment.
Prevent incident response itself from spreading sensitive personnel information beyond need-to-know staff.
Keep collection, containment, and dossier access within incident-response authorization.

T preserves evidence before any destructive recovery path
player understands MFA changes authentication confidence but does not prove endpoint integrity
vendor dependency is traced and treated as a risk boundary rather than assumed root cause
E protects privacy/access boundaries while preserving the incident workflow
squad acts appropriately under partial evidence and increases confidence through corroboration
player distinguishes containment, impact scoping, evidence preservation, and restoration as separate jobs

label: Global state authorization constraints
value: Incident team may access affected personnel-system records only for impact determination, containment, evidence preservation, and required notification.
Unrelated personal records are out of scope.
Destructive recovery is authorized only after preservation or explicit emergency justification.
Physical force is defensive and must remain consistent with the fictional mission threat state.

label: Implementation acceptance tests
value: Player can finish primary containment without firing a weapon, but doing so should require exceptional positioning/control.
Player can engage in a satisfying firefight without automatically completing any primary IT objective.
At least one optimal play path uses suppression rather than a kill attempt to buy T an anchored action.
R evidence must reduce T ambiguity in a mechanically visible way.
E Control must prevent at least one lab interruption or custody loss in ordinary play.
T verified containment must alter enemy or route behavior on the board.
Broad shutdown must be mechanically valid but create continuity/compliance tradeoffs.
An interrupted Preserve action must remain recoverable without restart.
Window expiration must transition to extraction with partial value rather than show an instant failure banner.
Debrief must be capable of pointing to the precise concept and lyric cue associated with every major technical mistake.

label: Proposed civilian baseline
value: Professional apartment, structured calendar, carefully chosen art, too many unread messages from people asking for decisions. A normal Tuesday is sponsor work, contract review, family voice notes, and one late hour spent rereading the risk section everybody else skimmed.

label: Proposed money family
value: Comfortable but not generationally wealthy. Family respects her career but does not understand why she sometimes disappears into work without explanation.
note: 14 — Amira Hassan — Egypt — 39

label: Proposed education specialty
value: Procurement, program management, technical contracting, mission sponsorship.
note: 14 — Amira Hassan — Egypt — 39

label: Proposed social presentation
value: Composed, diplomatic, capable of stopping a room without raising her voice. Attraction makes her more private. Disrespect makes her almost unnervingly courteous.

value: Controlled, concise, low profanity, asks “what are we actually authorizing?” often enough to annoy people.

label: Proposed desire
value: power with a functioning ethical brake.

label: Proposed fear

label: Proposed contradiction
value: excellent at refusing others, vulnerable to Prime's authority.

label: Proposed moral boundary
value: will not sign a mission she believes hides material risk from the team.
note: 14 — Amira Hassan — Egypt — 39

label: Proposed stress habit

note: 14 — Amira Hassan — Egypt — 39

label: Proposed secret
value: keeps copies of refusal rationales leadership wanted softened.
note: 14 — Amira Hassan — Egypt — 39

label: Proposed relationships
value: ethical counterweight to Marc; trusted by Helen; respected by Chioma; Prime tests whether her principles survive urgency.
note: 14 — Amira Hassan — Egypt — 39

label: Proposed failure mode
value: believing a clean authorization process can redeem a dirty objective.
note: 14 — Amira Hassan — Egypt — 39

note: 14 — Amira Hassan — Egypt — 39

label: Proposed civilian baseline
value: First-year college student, recently homeless, living as cheaply and close to campus/work as circumstances allow. A normal Tuesday before McCluster is class, library/computer-lab time, job hunting, fixing somebody else's tech for cash, checking account balance too often, and trying to look less financially unstable than he is.
note: 01 — McCluster — United States — 33

label: Proposed money family
value: Money is immediate, not abstract. He thinks in bus fare, food, tuition, phone service, storage, and whether he can afford to say no to an opportunity. Family ties exist but he hates becoming another emergency somebody has to solve.
note: 01 — McCluster — United States — 33

label: Proposed education specialty
value: Years of practical IT, infrastructure and data-center work; formally under-credentialed. Strongest at systems diagnosis, infrastructure intuition and recognizing when official descriptions do not match operational reality.
note: 01 — McCluster — United States — 33

label: Proposed social presentation
value: Older freshman energy: observant, capable, sometimes defensive when younger classmates assume age equals authority or failure. He often makes jokes right before admitting something serious.
note: 01 — McCluster — United States — 33

label: Proposed voice
value: Medium-short sentences, concrete examples, technical slang only when useful, moderate profanity, answers directly unless the question touches shame or dependency. Talks more when excited about a system; less when embarrassed about money.
note: 01 — McCluster — United States — 33

label: Proposed private wound
value: Years of being useful without being institutionally secure. Being treated as disposable hurts more than he admits.
note: 01 — McCluster — United States — 33

label: Proposed desire
value: legitimacy and control over his future.
note: 01 — McCluster — United States — 33

label: Proposed fear
value: becoming powerful enough to never be disposable and then treating others as disposable.
note: 01 — McCluster — United States — 33

label: Proposed contradiction
value: deeply distrusts institutions while craving recognition from one.
note: 01 — McCluster — United States — 33

label: Proposed moral boundary
value: believes he would never knowingly sacrifice a teammate for institutional efficiency.
note: 01 — McCluster — United States — 33

label: Proposed stress habit
value: stops sleeping, over-researches, starts treating every problem like it can be solved if he just refuses to quit.
note: 01 — McCluster — United States — 33

label: Proposed secret
value: he sometimes needs McCluster to be good because admitting it may be dangerous would mean the best opportunity of his life is another trap.
note: 01 — McCluster — United States — 33

label: Proposed relationships
value: trusts Aya; protects Valeria; is professionally dependent on Chioma and Arjun earlier than he likes; underestimates Grace's ability to read him; Prime sees through him from the beginning.
note: 01 — McCluster — United States — 33

label: Proposed failure mode
note: 01 — McCluster — United States — 33

label: Proposed longevity
note: 01 — McCluster — United States — 33

label: Proposed test
value: whether he can become Prime without converting love, grief and friendship into resource accounting.

label: Function
value:
The highest institutional human identity on the Prime side. EI-01 holds strategic control and final institutional weight. This is not an operator, not a facility guard, and not a program manager. This is the person whose decisions shape what programs exist, what risks are acceptable, and whether the succession path itself continues to mean anything.

EI-01 is rare. Most people in the system will never be in a room with one. When they are, the room changes.

label: Place in institutional authority triad
value:
| ID | Name | Focus |
|----|------|--------|
| **EI-01** | Executive Authority | Strategic control, final institutional weight |
| **EI-02** | Program / Operations Director | Machinery — programs, resources, tempo |
| **EI-03** | Mission Sponsor | Accountability for a specific line of effort |

EI-01 sets intent.  
EI-02 turns intent into portfolio reality.  
EI-03 owns a single line and answers for it.

label: Visual direction locked
value:
From executive identity canon:

1. Modern black single-breasted, two-button suit with notch lapels
2. Matching black tailored trousers with side adjusters and no belt
3. Warm ivory-white executive shirt
4. Plain black silk tie
5. Exact McCluster M as a small jewelry-grade left-lapel pin
6. Two separate horizontal red enamel stripes as the tie clip itself (no visible carrier bar)
7. Dark oxblood-brown wingtip shoes

**Reads as:** modern American authority and private-client wealth — not retail luxury, streetwear, tactical clothing, or ceremonial costume.

### Hard visual exclusions
- Double-breasted jacket, peak-lapel ceremony styling
- Loud monogram surface, printed tie motif, oversized branding
- Pocket square, belt, watch, chain as identity gear
- Tactical equipment of any kind
- Bright tan shoes
- Additional visible accessories beyond the locked system

Source asset: `assets/canon/brands/mccluster-corp/executive-identity/MCC-EI-01-modern-executive-horizontal-two-stripe-clip-v01.jpg`

label: Equipment presence ceiling
value:

- No cyberdeck as visible kit
- No FO or SOI gear
- Authority is carried by cut, mark placement, stillness, and access — not by tools
- May operate through secure terminals and briefings; the body remains executive, not technical

label: Core responsibilities
value:
- Set and protect institutional direction
- Decide which classes of risk the organization will accept
- Appoint, constrain, or remove EI-02 / EI-03 weight
- Hold the meaning of the succession path (including PRIME-N1) as an institutional fact, not a personal favor
- Absorb or redirect political consequence that would otherwise break the lower system
- Remain the final human authority inside McCluster-controlled logic

label: Behavioral expectations
value:
### Core posture
An EI-01 does not rush. Movement, speech, and attention are rationed. The phenotype signals that time and access are the scarce resources, not force.

### Decision logic
- Thinks in decades and institutional survival, not single missions
- Will accept operational loss to preserve structural integrity
- Will accept structural change only when the alternative is institutional death or capture
- Treats people as both necessary and replaceable — this is the central moral tension of the role
- Rarely reverses a decision in public; adjusts through EI-02 machinery instead

### Relationship to the rest of the system
| Layer | Relationship |
|-------|----------------|
| EI-02 | Issues intent; expects portfolio translation without constant supervision |
| EI-03 | Distant; sees sponsors as instruments and liability surfaces |
| CO-03 / Field | Almost never direct; when direct contact happens it is decisive or ceremonial |
| SOI / BS-01 | Assumes the building and its defense function; intervenes only when continuity is threatened |
| PRIME-N1 | Institutional counterpart in the succession domain — different axis of power, same altitude |

### Speech
- Short when possible; precise when necessary
- Does not explain tactics
- Does not perform empathy for effect; when warmth appears it is intentional and rare
- Questions are often more important than statements

### Presence rules
- Physical appearance in operator spaces is an event
- Physical appearance in Building Defense spaces is an inspection or crisis
- Most influence is exercised through absence — through what EI-02 is allowed to fund and what EI-03 is allowed to own

label: Psychological load ei 01 specific
value:
- Isolation at the top of a system that eats people
- Responsibility for outcomes executed by others under conditions EI-01 will never fully feel
- Knowledge that succession and evaluation logic may one day apply pressure back upward
- The requirement to remain legible as authority while never becoming merely a mascot of power
- Chronic tension between institutional immortality and human cost

label: Failure modes
value:
- Becoming ornamental — marks and suit without actual decision rights
- Micromanaging EI-02/EI-03 until the machinery freezes
- Treating the cohort as pure consumable and hollowing loyalty until the system cannot recruit or retain
- Capturing the succession path as personal loyalty instead of institutional mechanism
- Disappearing so completely that EI-02 becomes the real executive without accountability

label: Social signal
value: “I do not run the door. I decide whether the building, the programs, and the path continue to exist.”

label: Distinction from prime n1
value:
| EI-01 | PRIME-N1 |
|-------|----------|
| Institutional / corporate strategic authority | Operator succession end-state |
| Suit as identity | Full operator identity (M-helmet, Mission Core ceiling) |
| Power through programs and appointment | Power through operational mastery and succession |
| Rarely kinetic | Defined by operational capability |
| Protects the institution’s continuity | Embodies the institution’s sharp edge |

They can coexist. They are not the same phenotype and not the same career track by default.

label: Trifecta utility
value:
- **Game:** Top-authority layer; unlocks or freezes entire mission families; endgame political actor; rare interactable presence with outsized consequence
- **Story:** The face of the system’s will; source of pressure that cannot be punched; seasonal arcs about legitimacy, succession, and institutional sin
- **Real:** Board-level / principal executive function in a high-accountability private institution — strategy, risk appetite, appointment power, continuity

label: Transition
value:
- Entry into EI-01 is not the operator succession path. It is institutional power succession — rarer, more political, less kinetic.
- Exceptional EI-02 may rise.
- Operator-track individuals do not automatically become EI-01 by surviving the field.
- Exit is loss of legitimacy, forced removal, or institutional collapse — not a lateral move into FO kit.

value:
The operational executive. Turns strategic intent from EI-01 into runnable programs, resource allocation, schedules, and constraints. This is the suit who makes missions possible or impossible. Not the final authority. Not the person operators usually see on the objective. The institutional middle power that keeps the machinery aligned with executive direction.

If EI-01 decides *whether the institution continues*, EI-02 decides *what the institution is actually doing this quarter*.

label: Place in institutional authority triad
value:
| ID | Name | Focus |
|----|------|--------|
| **EI-01** | Executive Authority | Strategic control, final institutional weight |
| **EI-02** | Program / Operations Director | Machinery — programs, resources, tempo |
| **EI-03** | Mission Sponsor | Accountability for a specific line of effort |

label: Visual direction
value:
- Full corporate authority language (Authority Black or elevated Corporate Fits)
- Cleaner and more operational than pure boardroom EI-01; still unmistakably suit, never field
- Restrained Dual Sight / exact M marks — institutional, not operator
- No tactical armor, no FO kits, no SOI vest as primary identity
- No sidearm as identity gear
- May appear in secure ops spaces, program briefings, and controlled facility zones
- Silhouette reads: “I control the pipeline, not the door.”

### Distinction from EI-01 visually
EI-01 is private-client final authority — jewelry-grade stillness.  
EI-02 is the same language under load: slightly more present in working spaces, still never tactical, never casual.

### Hard exclusions
- Operator or Building Defense kits as identity
- Visible technical exploitation tools
- Loud branding, streetwear, or ceremonial costume
- Performing “one of the team” by putting on FO gear for optics

label: Core responsibilities
value:
- Translate EI-01 intent into funded, scheduled, constrained programs
- Allocate and withhold capacity across cohort, field, building defense, and sustainment
- Set the operational boundaries CO-03 must operate inside
- Approve or deny tempo at the program level
- Absorb and filter upward reporting before it reaches EI-01
- Hold EI-03 sponsors to delivery and risk standards
- Protect institutional continuity when individual missions fail
- Decide which mission families exist this cycle — and which do not

label: Behavioral expectations
value:
### Core posture
An EI-02 moves like someone who is always trading. Every yes to one line of effort is a no to another. They live in capacity, risk, and schedule — not in the romance of the objective.

### Decision logic
- Speaks in programs, risk, and continuity — not individual heroics
- Will sacrifice a single mission to protect a larger line of effort
- Will open tempo when the institution can absorb the cost
- Will freeze tempo when the cohort is being consumed faster than it can be replaced
- Evaluates CO-03 leads as hard as the missions they run
- Does not need to be liked by the operators; needs the pipeline to function

### Relationship to the system
| Layer | Relationship |
|-------|----------------|
| **EI-01** | Receives intent; returns portfolio reality and filtered risk |
| **EI-03** | Assigns, constrains, and holds sponsors accountable |
| **CO-03** | Sets the box the lead must operate inside; rarely micromanages the door |
| **Field triad** | Almost never direct; exists as capacity numbers and outcome reports |
| **SOI / BS-01** | Assumes facility continuity; intervenes when programs depend on building state |
| **PRIME-N1** | Coordinates at altitude when succession ops and program ops collide |

### Speech
- Precise, capacity-aware, short on narrative
- Uses “we can / we cannot absorb” more than “we should”
- Does not brief tactics to feel involved
- When cutting a program or freezing a team, language is clean and final

### Presence rules
- More visible than EI-01 in program and ops spaces
- Still an event when appearing in pure operator work areas
- Most power is exercised through schedules, funding, and what is allowed on the board — not through walking the floor

label: Psychological load ei 02 specific
value:
- Permanent middle position: pressure from EI-01 above, resistance and human cost from below
- Responsibility for outcomes executed by people EI-02 will never fully know
- The knowledge that “protecting the program” sometimes means ending a team’s work mid-arc
- Career identity tied to portfolio health, not personal operational glory
- Temptation to manage the story of capacity instead of the reality of attrition

label: Failure modes
value:
- Becoming a pure relay — passing EI-01 intent without adding real constraint or judgment
- Capturing power by starving EI-03 and CO-03 of clarity until only EI-02 can decide
- Over-identifying with one sponsor or one team and distorting the whole portfolio
- Freezing too late after the cohort is already hollowed
- Opening tempo to look decisive while the institution cannot replace what it is burning
- Performing closeness to operators without accepting their constraints

label: Social signal
value: “I do not own the mission. I own whether the mission is allowed to exist.”

- **Story:** Face of “the system decided.” Institutional politics without requiring EI-01 in every scene. Pressure that is procedural and lethal at the same time.
- **Real:** Program director / senior operations executive in a high-accountability organization — portfolio delivery, resource arbitration, risk absorption between strategy and execution.

- Lateral move into pure staff or exit is more common than upward movement

label: Core responsibilities
value:

- Receive CO-03 after-action truth and convert it into institutional reporting
- Protect or expose the team upward depending on standards, politics, and self-preservation
- Absorb political and career consequence when the line succeeds or fails
- Stay close enough to understand the work without becoming an operator
- Push for resources from EI-02 without promising the team what the portfolio cannot give

label: Behavioral expectations
value:
### Core posture
An EI-03 lives closer to the heat than the other suits. They still do not take field risk as identity, but their career is tied to outcomes executed by people who do. They are the human hinge between the cohort’s reality and the institution’s story of that reality.

### Decision logic
- More available to CO-03 than EI-02 or EI-01
- Under pressure, may push for results harder than the team can safely deliver — known failure mode
- Can become the team’s shield **or** the team’s problem
- Must choose, repeatedly, whether to transmit the team’s truth upward or manage the narrative
- Wins by delivering the line; loses by either burning the team or failing the objective

### Relationship to the system
| Layer | Relationship |
|-------|----------------|
| **EI-01** | Distant source of legitimacy; rarely direct |
| **EI-02** | Immediate institutional boss for resources and permission |
| **CO-03** | Primary working relationship; mutual dependence and mutual danger |
| **Field triad** | Feels them as “the suit who sent us”; rarely present on objective |
| **SOI / BS-01** | Uses facility as assumed background unless the line depends on it |

### Speech
- Mixes operational detail with institutional framing
- More concrete than EI-02; less absolute than EI-01
- In briefings: clear objective, accepted risk, constraints
- After action: either the cleanest translator of CO-03’s truth — or the first editor of it

### Presence rules
- Most present of the three suits in operator-adjacent spaces
- Still an institutional event when entering pure field recovery or intimate cohort space
- Post-mission sessions are where EI-03 is most dangerous and most useful

- Career and identity tied to outcomes they do not personally execute
- Temptation to manage the story of the mission rather than the reality
- Tension between loyalty to operators and loyalty to the institution that judges them
- Proximity without shared risk — the moral hazard of the role
- Knowing that protecting the team can look like failure upward, and protecting upward can look like betrayal downward

label: Failure modes

- Becoming pure pressure — extracting results until the element breaks
- Becoming pure advocate — losing institutional credibility and thus the ability to resource the team
- Editing after-action truth until EI-02/EI-01 operate on fiction
- Using the team’s loyalty as personal political capital
- Disappearing after failure and leaving CO-03 to carry both the operational and political cost
- Performing solidarity in the room and abandonment in the report

label: Behavioral expectations
value:
### Core posture
A CO-01 operator moves like someone who has already accepted that the next mission might remove them from the story permanently. They are competent enough to be useful and still human enough to be afraid. The fear is managed, not absent.

### Competence and limitation
- They execute tasks with professional focus but still reveal gaps in experience.
- They do not possess the near-omniscient systems intuition of the presiding Prime.
- When something unexpected happens, the first visible response is rapid assessment, not panic or bravado.
- They will attempt improvisation when doctrine fails, but the improvisation is still grounded in training rather than pure genius.

### Relationship to hierarchy
- They treat the institution as both employer and judge.
- Orders from above are followed with visible discipline, even when private doubt exists.
- They watch the people above them carefully — not only for instruction, but for survival cues.
- Open defiance is rare. Quiet, private re-evaluation of loyalty is constant.

### Relationship to the cohort
- Teammates are simultaneously the only people who understand the pressure and potential future liabilities.
- Genuine care for specific individuals coexists with the knowledge that the system may later require them to treat those same people as resources or risks.
- After a mission that produces attrition, the remaining operators show restrained grief mixed with heightened vigilance. They do not perform dramatic mourning in front of the institution.
- Humor, when it appears, is dry, short-lived, and usually directed at shared absurdity rather than at each other.

### Relationship to the mission
- They treat every operational problem as both a technical challenge and an evaluation event.
- Success is noted but not celebrated for long. Failure is studied immediately.
- They document and report with unusual precision because incomplete records are dangerous.
- They understand that “mission success” and “personal survival” are related but not identical goals.

### Emotional texture
- Fatigue is visible in posture and micro-expressions even when the operator is fully functional.
- Emotional range is compressed: fewer big displays, more controlled intensity.
- Moments of private doubt are allowed; public collapse is not.
- The operator is learning to separate what they feel from what the system needs them to do. This separation is incomplete and costly.

### Speech and communication
- Language is more precise and less casual than civilian or early-recruit speech.
- Technical terms appear naturally because they are tools, not performance.
- They avoid unnecessary speculation about the true nature of the organization in mixed company.
- When speaking to the presiding Prime or senior evaluators, economy of words becomes extreme.

### Failure modes (behavioral)
- Over-identification with the cohort at the expense of institutional survival instincts.
- Premature hardening that makes them treat teammates as already expendable.
- Paralysis when the cost of a correct action is the loss of a specific person they still care about.
- Quiet accumulation of resentment toward the evaluation process itself.

### What the audience should feel
Watching a CO-01 operator should produce a mixture of respect and dread. They are no longer outsiders, but they are also not yet the finished product. Every mission is simultaneously work and a test they cannot fully see the grading criteria for.

label: Psychological trauma profile
value:
CO-01 trauma is not cinematic breakdown. It is the slow, functional damage produced by repeated exposure to low-probability survival conditions while still being required to perform at a high level. The system does not break operators cleanly. It wears specific parts of them down while leaving the rest operational.

### Primary trauma sources

1. **Attrition of the known**  
   Watching specific people the operator trained, ate, and argued with simply stop existing. The institution frames these losses in sterile language. The operator is left holding the human version of the event with no official place to put it.

2. **Evaluation under lethal conditions**  
   Every mission is simultaneously a real operation and a graded test. The operator cannot fully separate “I am trying to keep us alive” from “I am being measured.” This dual frame creates chronic hyper-vigilance and a background sense that survival itself is being scored.

3. **Moral injury through procedure**  
   The operator is required to follow systems and orders that produce outcomes they would not have chosen as a private individual. The damage is not usually from a single monstrous act, but from the accumulation of smaller, justified decisions that erode the operator’s previous moral map.

4. **Anticipatory loss**  
   Once the operator understands the statistical reality of the work, they begin grieving people who are still alive. This anticipatory grief is quiet, continuous, and rarely spoken.

5. **Identity compression**  
   The civilian self, the student self, and the operator self are forced into the same body. Over time the operator experiences a progressive narrowing of who they are allowed to be in public and, eventually, in private.

### Observable trauma signatures

- **Sleep architecture changes**: light, interrupted, or highly scheduled sleep. Difficulty returning to rest after high-arousal events.
- **Emotional blunting with selective intensity**: reduced reactivity to ordinary stimuli, paired with sudden sharp responses to specific triggers (certain names, locations, equipment sounds, the smell of a particular environment).
- **Hyper-responsibility**: the operator privately assigns themselves more causal weight for outcomes than is accurate or fair.
- **Ritualized competence**: small, repeated technical or preparatory actions performed with unnecessary precision as a way of restoring a sense of control.
- **Social withdrawal that still looks professional**: the operator remains functional in team settings but reduces voluntary closeness. New bonds form more slowly and with more internal resistance.
- **Survivor’s accounting**: after attrition events, the operator runs silent internal ledgers of who lived, who did not, and what variables might explain the difference. This accounting is rarely shared.

### Internal contradictions the trauma produces

- The need for the cohort as the only people who understand the pressure *versus* the growing knowledge that attachment itself is a liability under the system’s rules.
- The desire to remain human *versus* the recognition that remaining fully human may reduce the probability of surviving long enough to matter.
- Loyalty to specific individuals *versus* loyalty to the institutional path that is the only route to greater agency.
- The hunger for recognition of competence *versus* the fear that greater competence simply means harder and more lethal assignments.

### Progressive stages (typical, not universal)

**Stage 1 — Acute exposure**  
After the first real attrition event. Shock is present but often masked by technical focus. The operator may over-work and under-sleep. Language becomes more precise as a stabilizing mechanism.

**Stage 2 — Functional adaptation**  
The operator develops reliable external performance while the internal cost rises. Emotional range compresses. Humor becomes drier. The operator begins to anticipate loss before it occurs.

**Stage 3 — Structural change**  
Attachment patterns shift. The operator may still care deeply but invests less freely. Decision-making becomes more utilitarian under pressure. The civilian moral framework is no longer the default; it must be deliberately retrieved.

**Stage 4 — Pre-succession hardening (late)**  
If the operator continues long enough, the capacity required to approach the succession path begins to form. This is not the same as becoming evil. It is the gradual acceptance that the system’s final logic may require the operator to treat even valued people as obstacles or variables. The trauma here is the quiet recognition of what they are becoming capable of.

### What the trauma is not

- It is not constant visible distress.
- It is not automatic moral collapse.
- It is not a single defining nightmare sequence.
- It is not resolved by a single conversation or cathartic moment.

The damage is cumulative, often invisible to outsiders, and frequently mistaken by the institution for successful adaptation.

### Narrative utility

CO-01 trauma is the primary engine that turns competent recruits into people capable of the later story. It explains why tenacity matters more than brilliance: the operators who continue are not the ones who feel the least, but the ones who can keep moving while carrying the weight. The same process that damages them is also the process that forges the capacity the succession path eventually requires.

label: Gear specifications
value:
### Design philosophy
FO-01 gear is **mission-configured institutional equipment**.  
It must remain clearly McCluster in silhouette, materials, and marks while accepting that the field is hostile, dirty, and unpredictable.  
Mobility and modularity outrank heavy protection.  
Every added item must justify its weight and visual noise.

### Equipment Floor (minimum viable FO-01)
Every Field Operator deploys with at least:

| Item | Specification |
|------|---------------|
| Base layer | Dark technical under-suit / combat shirt and trousers, matte finish |
| Armor | Soft-to-mid protective vest or light plate carrier; torso coverage only |
| Sidearm | One compact service sidearm in low-profile retention holster |
| Comms | Secure team radio + bone or in-ear element |
| Recording | Body-worn or helmet/headset-mounted mission recorder |
| Compute | Field cyberdeck or advanced wrist module with offline capability |
| Identification | Visible Dual Sight or red `//` accent for rapid friendly recognition |
| Footwear | Rugged, quiet-soled boots rated for extended wear and mixed terrain |
| Handwear | Tactical gloves compatible with device use and weapon handling |

### Equipment Ceiling (authorized maximum)
The following may be added according to mission profile. Nothing beyond this list is standard.

**Protection**
- Soft armor with optional thin hard plates (front/back only)
- Limited extremity protection (knees, elbows) only when the environment demands it
- Neck or lower-face protection short of a full helmet
- No full ballistic helmet, no riot gear, no bomb suit derivatives

**Head / Face**
- Advanced tactical headset with integrated comms and recording
- Partial protective shell or reinforced balaclava
- Low-profile eye protection / visor
- **Forbidden:** full M-architecture helmet and Mission Core (PRIME-N1 only)

**Core Electronics**
- Field cyberdeck (larger than SOI version, still wearable)
- Redundant encrypted communications
- Mission recording suite (body + optional weapon or tool mount)
- Compact power bank / hot-swap battery system
- Limited electronic countermeasure or signal analysis module (mission-specific)

**Mission Modules** (attach only what the operation requires)
- Technical entry / bypass kit
- Breaching charge or mechanical entry tools (when authorized)
- Surveillance / sensor package
- Forensic imaging or data-extraction tools
- Short-range drone or throwable sensor (rare, high-value missions only)
- Medical blowout kit (individual)
- Signaling and marking devices

**Lethal / Decisive Tools**
- One sidearm (mandatory floor)
- One primary tool or weapon appropriate to the specific task (carbine, suppressed platform, or specialized technical tool)
- No standard issue long gun across the entire phenotype; weapon is mission-selected
- No visible spare magazine farms or excessive external pouches that turn the silhouette into conventional infantry

### Modular Logic
Gear is attached to a clean base chassis (vest + belt + optional light pack).  
Modules are added or removed per mission.  
An operator returning from a technical infiltration should not look identical to one returning from a contested extraction.  
The base identity (silhouette, marks, color language) remains constant; only the modules change.

### Marks & Identity Hardware
- Exact McCluster M appears in restrained, durable form (subdued or tonal preferred in field)
- Dual Sight and/or red `//` must remain readable for team identification in low light
- No non-McCluster patches, flags, or unit insignia
- No morale patches or personalization that breaks institutional uniformity

### Exclusions (hard)
- Full Prime M-helmet + Jetson-class Mission Core
- Clean Corporate Fits (CFI) office garments
- Conventional military plate carriers overloaded with pouches
- Visible ammunition management systems that dominate the silhouette
- Riot shields, batons as primary, or crowd-control equipment
- Any gear that makes the operator read as generic special forces or police SWAT
- Non-canon marks or commercial branding

### Comparison Snapshot

| Element | SOI-01 Security | CO-01 Standard | FO-01 Field |
|---------|------------------|----------------|-------------|
| Domain | Facility | Institutional / mixed | External / uncontrolled |
| Armor | Ultra-thin vest | Light soft armor | Soft-to-mid, modular |
| Primary weapon | Sidearm only | Sidearm + limited tool | Sidearm + mission-selected primary |
| Electronics | Cyberdeck | Wrist module / light compute | Full field cyberdeck + redundant comms |
| Recording | Body camera | Body / mission recorder | Full mission recording suite |
| Modules | Almost none | Minimal | Mission-configured |
| Environmental rating | Indoor / campus | Mixed | Full field |
| Visual noise | Lowest | Low | Controlled but higher |

### Load-bearing principles
1. If the item is not required for the specific mission, it is left behind.
2. Every external pouch or module must earn its place visually and functionally.
3. The operator must still be able to move, climb, enter confined spaces, and operate devices without fighting their own gear.
4. When in doubt, the silhouette should still say “McCluster institutional operator,” not “soldier.”

label: Social signal
value: “We are no longer inside the system’s walls. The environment is hostile and the evaluation continues.”

label: Behavioral expectations
value:
### Core posture
A Field Operator moves with the understanding that the environment itself is an active variable. Unlike facility work, the field does not care about institutional procedure. The operator must remain institutional while the world refuses to cooperate.

### Operational behavior
- Higher baseline arousal than CO-01 inside the building
- Faster decision loops; less time for perfect information
- Strong preference for reversible actions until the point of no return
- Explicit contingency thinking (“if this node fails, we move to…”)
- Reduced tolerance for internal debate once the team is exposed

### Relationship to the environment
- Treats architecture, networks, weather, civilians, and local forces as part of the problem set
- Constant low-level scanning for surveillance, ambush, and technical compromise
- Willingness to abandon gear or change plans when the environment demands it

### Relationship to the team
- Tighter physical and communicative spacing than in facility operations
- Clearer role specialization under pressure
- Faster assumption of leadership if the designated lead is degraded
- After contact or loss, the remaining operators re-stabilize the team before processing emotion

### Psychological load (field-specific)
- Isolation from institutional support structures
- Increased moral complexity when operating among civilians or under foreign legal regimes
- Greater anticipatory stress because extraction is not guaranteed
- The knowledge that failure in the field is harder to conceal or reframe than failure inside a McCluster facility

### Speech and communication
- Shorter transmissions
- Higher use of procedural and brevity codes
- Minimal speculation once the operation is live
- After-action language becomes extremely precise; emotional content is deferred

| Dimension | SOI-01 Security Officer | FO-01 Field Operator |
|-----------|-------------------------|----------------------|
| Domain | Inside / around McCluster facilities | External, uncontrolled environments |
| Primary mission | Protect people, data, continuity | Execute directed external objectives |
| Threat model | Internal breach, access control, cyber | Hostile actors, environment, surveillance, kinetic |
| Gear philosophy | Minimal, professional, cyber-first | Modular, mission-configured, higher risk tolerance |
| Visual signal | Corporate security | Institutional operator in the open world |

It is what the audience sees during government-directed missions, data-center raids, infrastructure operations, and any sequence where the cohort is operating against a real external adversary. It keeps the McCluster institutional signal while acknowledging that the field is a different, more lethal classroom.

label: Function
value:
The physical access and close-security specialist. Responsible for getting the team onto the objective, controlling immediate space, and protecting the Technical operator while the technical work is performed. This is the kinetic and spatial problem-solver of the field triad.

FO-E exists so that FO-T can work. When the technical window is open, FO-E’s primary product is controlled space and time.

label: Visual direction
value:
- Highest soft-to-mid armor load of the three basic field phenotypes
- Darker, more aggressive weathering than FO-T; still institutional, never generic special forces
- Strong, readable Dual Sight / red `//` for rapid recognition in confined spaces, smoke, or low light
- Silhouette emphasizes mobility + protection rather than maximum armor bulk
- Gloves and boots built for forced movement, climbing, door work, and close contact
- Face protection short of the full M-helmet (partial shell, reinforced balaclava, or advanced headset)
- Overall look: the person who goes through the door first and holds it

label: Gear specifications
value:
### Design philosophy
Gear exists to create access, hold space, and keep FO-T alive and working.  
Every added item must improve entry, control, or protection.  
Bulk that slows movement through doors, stairs, or confined plant rooms is rejected.

### Equipment Floor
| Item | Specification |
|------|---------------|
| Base layer | Dark technical field suit |
| Armor | Soft-to-mid torso protection; highest of the triad |
| Sidearm | One compact service sidearm, low-profile holster |
| Primary | Mission-selected primary tool or weapon (more common than on FO-T) |
| Entry tools | Mechanical entry set at minimum |
| Comms | Secure team radio + reliable earpiece |
| Recording | Body or headset mission recorder |
| Identification | Strong Dual Sight or red `//` visibility |
| Handwear | Impact- and abrasion-resistant gloves that still allow device and weapon use |
| Footwear | Aggressive field boots rated for forced movement and debris |

### Equipment Ceiling (mission-authorized)
**Protection**
- Soft armor with optional thin hard plates (front/back)
- Limited extremity protection (knees, elbows) when the environment demands it
- Partial face / neck protection
- No full ballistic helmet, no riot gear, no bomb-suit derivatives

**Entry & Access**
- Mechanical entry tools (spreaders, breachers, bypass hardware)
- Limited energetic entry tools when authorized
- Door and lock defeat capability appropriate to the target
- Short-range cutting or penetration tools for interior obstacles

**Kinetic**
- Sidearm mandatory
- Mission-selected primary (carbine, suppressed platform, or specialized entry weapon)
- No magazine-farm infantry setups that destroy the institutional silhouette

**Electronics**
- Standard field comms and recording
- Limited personal sensor or short-range detection tools
- No full technical exploitation stack (that belongs to FO-T)

### Hard Exclusions
- Full Prime M-helmet and Mission Core
- Heavy plate carriers overloaded with pouches
- Primary technical exploitation kits (FO-T domain)
- Long-duration observation / sniper-style optics packages (FO-R domain)
- Clean Corporate Fits garments
- Non-McCluster marks or generic special-forces patches

---

label: Gear loadouts by mission profile
value:
FO-E does not wear one fixed kit. The base identity stays constant; modules change with the phase of the operation. Below are the four primary loadout configurations.

### 1. Approach & Entry (FO-E-AE)
**Use when:** Moving to the objective and making the initial breach or technical entry.

| Category | Load |
|----------|------|
| Armor | Soft-to-mid torso; optional thin plates |
| Entry tools | Full mechanical set + limited energetic if authorized |
| Kinetic | Sidearm + mission-selected primary |
| Comms | Full secure team link |
| Recording | Continuous from final approach |
| Identification | Strong Dual Sight / `//` visibility |
| Mobility | Balanced — must carry entry tools without becoming slow in corridors |

**Design note:** This is FO-E at its most tool-heavy. The job is to open the space. Once inside and the door is controlled, excess entry tools can be staged or dropped if they interfere with holding.

---

### 2. Hold & Protect (FO-E-HP)
**Use when:** FO-T is on the target node and FO-E is pure close security — doors, angles, and immediate space.

| Category | Load |
|----------|------|
| Armor | Soft-to-mid; prioritize coverage over tool bulk |
| Entry tools | Minimal — only what is still needed for interior obstacles |
| Kinetic | Sidearm + primary ready; emphasis on control, not volume of fire |
| Comms | Full link to FO-T and FO-R |
| Recording | Continuous |
| Identification | High visibility for rapid team recognition in confined space |
| Mobility | High within the held space; must be able to shift rooms or collapse fast |

**Design note:** Stripped of pure entry bulk. The product is controlled space and time. Every extra pouch that slows a room-to-room shift is a liability.

---

### 3. Contact / Collapse (FO-E-CC)
**Use when:** The space is compromised, contact has occurred, or FO-R has called an external threat that forces movement.

| Category | Load |
|----------|------|
| Armor | Maximum authorized soft-to-mid for FO-E |
| Entry tools | Only what is required for the exit path |
| Kinetic | Sidearm + primary; readiness for short, decisive action |
| Comms | High-tempo team link |
| Recording | Continuous through the break-contact |
| Identification | High visibility — team must find each other under stress |
| Mobility | Highest priority — lead the move, keep FO-T moving, break contact |

**Design note:** This is FO-E in emergency mode. Entry tools become secondary. The job is no longer “hold for the technical window”; it is “get the protected asset and the team off the objective alive.”

---

### 4. Technical Escort (FO-E-TE)
**Use when:** Moving FO-T between nodes inside a larger facility, or escorting the technical element during a multi-stage objective where entry is already complete but the space is still hostile.

| Category | Load |
|----------|------|
| Armor | Soft-to-mid, balanced for movement with FO-T |
| Entry tools | Light interior set (doors, cabinets, secondary barriers) |
| Kinetic | Sidearm + compact primary preferred |
| Comms | Tight link to FO-T; FO-R picture still active |
| Recording | Continuous |
| Identification | Readable Dual Sight |
| Mobility | Matched to FO-T’s pace — never so light that protection is sacrificed, never so heavy that FO-T is delayed |

**Design note:** Hybrid of Hold and movement. FO-E stays glued to the technical element without turning the pair into a slow, over-armored target.

---

### Loadout Selection Logic

| Situation | Preferred Loadout |
|-----------|-------------------|
| Final approach and initial breach | Approach & Entry (FO-E-AE) |
| FO-T working, space still tenable | Hold & Protect (FO-E-HP) |
| Contact, FO-R abort call, or space lost | Contact / Collapse (FO-E-CC) |
| Moving FO-T between interior nodes | Technical Escort (FO-E-TE) |

An operator will typically sequence through these in a single mission: Approach & Entry → Hold & Protect → (optional Technical Escort) → Contact/Collapse or controlled exit.

### Cross-loadout rules
1. Sidearm never comes off.
2. Dual Sight stays readable unless a specific low-signature phase is ordered (rare for FO-E).
3. No loadout may become a full technical exploitation kit or a pure long-range observation package.
4. If the operator cannot move through a standard door or stairwell under control, the loadout is wrong for FO-E.
5. When FO-T is exposed and working, FO-E’s kit must not create noise, snag, or delay that endangers the technical window.

---

label: Core responsibilities
value:
- Route selection and physical approach
- Forced or technical entry onto the objective
- Immediate area security once inside
- Close protection of FO-T during the entire technical window
- Control of doors, corridors, stairs, and chokepoints
- Leading movement on contact or emergency exfiltration
- Rapid decision-making about whether the space is still tenable

label: Behavioral expectations
value:
### Core posture
An Entry Field Operator treats space as a resource that is constantly being spent. Every second the door is open, every corridor left unsecured, and every angle left uncovered is a cost. The job is to buy FO-T enough controlled space and time to finish the work.

### During entry and on the objective
- Highest baseline physical readiness on the team
- Decisions are spatial and temporal: where to stand, what to block, when to move, when to collapse the perimeter
- Low tolerance for extended technical debate once the team is exposed
- Treats FO-T as a protected asset for the duration of the technical window
- Maintains constant awareness of FO-R’s external picture

### On contact or deterioration
- Prioritizes team integrity and exit over continued objective work unless explicitly ordered otherwise
- Will force movement if the space becomes indefensible
- Does not require perfect information to act; acts on the best available picture and updates in motion

### Speech patterns
- Short, directional, and action-oriented
- Uses clear movement and security language
- Minimal narrative while the situation is live
- After contact, language becomes extremely precise about what happened in the space and what the remaining options are

### Relationship to pressure
- External threat increases tempo rather than producing hesitation
- Visible stress appears as sharper movement and shorter communications
- The operator is expected to remain the calmest body in the room when the room becomes violent

label: Psychological load fo e specific
value:
- Responsibility for the physical survival of the technical element
- The knowledge that a single bad angle or delayed movement can erase the entire technical take and the people who produced it
- Repeated exposure to the moment of entry — the highest-risk transition in most operations
- Carrying the immediate human cost when contact occurs (FO-T may still be focused on systems; FO-E is focused on bodies and space)
- Tendency toward hyper-vigilance about doors, corners, and timing that can persist after return to controlled environments

label: Relationship to the field triad
value:
| Phenotype | Relationship to FO-E |
|-----------|----------------------|
| FO-T Technical | Protected asset; FO-E’s primary product is the space and time FO-T needs |
| FO-R Recon | Supplies the external warning that lets FO-E decide whether the space is still worth holding |
| FO-E Entry | Creates access, holds the interior, leads movement on contact or exit |

label: Failure modes
value:
- Over-focusing on the immediate room and losing the larger exit picture
- Holding a space past the point it is tenable because FO-T is not finished
- Excessive aggression that creates noise or casualties the mission cannot afford
- Under-communicating movement decisions so FO-T and FO-R lose the picture
- Post-mission difficulty standing down from continuous spatial threat assessment

label: Narrative utility
value: FO-E is the phenotype for forced entry, corridor tension, and the physical reality that surrounds technical work. It keeps field sequences kinetic and human without collapsing the team into generic special-forces aesthetics. The drama sits in the collision between the need to protect the technical window and the need to keep the team alive when the space turns against them.

label: Transition
value:
- From CO-01 or FO-01 when assigned the entry / close-security role on an external mission
- Back to CO-01 or Corporate Fits when returning to controlled environments
- Repeated FO-E exposure accelerates the physical and spatial components of the broader operator trauma profile, with particular emphasis on responsibility for other people’s bodies in confined, hostile space

label: Phenotype definition
value: Institutional visual/functional role package, not a biological trait.

label: Function
value:
The external awareness and early-warning specialist. Responsible for surveillance of the approach, perimeter, and surrounding environment while the rest of the team is on the objective. This phenotype owns the question: “What is about to happen to us from outside?”

FO-R exists so that FO-E and FO-T can stay focused inward. Their primary product is a continuous, accurate external picture and the authority to force a change of plan when that picture collapses.

label: Visual direction
value:
- Lightest armor of the three basic field phenotypes for maximum mobility and low visual/thermal signature
- Darker, more subdued weathering; prioritizes blending over presence
- Dual Sight / red `//` is present but controllable — can be muted or covered when signature must stay low
- Silhouette optimized for static or semi-static observation positions and rapid displacement
- Optics and sensor packages are the visual signature more than heavy armor or weapons
- Face protection minimal and low-profile (headset, soft cover, or partial shell only)
- Overall look: the person who is hard to see and harder to surprise

label: Gear specifications
value:
### Design philosophy
Gear exists to see farther, stay quieter, and move faster than the threat.  
Observation quality and signature management outrank armor and pure kinetic load.  
Every item must justify itself against the cost of being detected.

### Equipment Floor
| Item | Specification |
|------|---------------|
| Base layer | Dark technical field suit, low-signature materials |
| Armor | Lightest soft torso protection of the triad |
| Sidearm | One compact service sidearm, low-profile holster |
| Optics | Mission-appropriate observation optics |
| Sensors | Basic environmental / approach detection capability |
| Comms | Secure team radio + reliable low-profile earpiece |
| Recording | Observation and mission recording suite |
| Identification | Dual Sight or red `//` that can be subdued |
| Handwear | Low-bulk gloves compatible with optics and device use |
| Footwear | Quiet-soled field boots optimized for movement and static positions |

### Equipment Ceiling (mission-authorized)
**Observation & Sensors**
- Enhanced day/night optics
- Extended-duration observation tools
- Compact sensor packages (motion, acoustic, or simple RF as authorized)
- Recording systems optimized for long takes and evidence-quality capture

**Protection & Mobility**
- Light soft armor only
- Minimal extremity protection
- No heavy plates that increase signature or reduce displacement speed
- No full helmet

**Kinetic**
- Sidearm mandatory
- Longer weapon only when the specific overwatch role requires it
- No heavy infantry-style loadouts

**Electronics**
- Extended secure comms and relay capability when acting as the external node
- Limited personal navigation and timing tools
- No full technical exploitation stack (FO-T domain)
- No primary entry/breaching tools (FO-E domain)

### Hard Exclusions
- Full Prime M-helmet and Mission Core
- Heavy armor or plate carriers
- Primary technical exploitation kits
- Primary entry/breaching loads
- High-visibility Dual Sight configurations when the mission requires low signature
- Clean Corporate Fits garments
- Non-McCluster marks

---

label: Gear loadouts by mission profile
value:
FO-R does not wear one fixed kit. The base identity stays constant; modules change with the job. Below are the four primary loadout configurations.

### 1. Static Overwatch (FO-R-SO)
**Use when:** The team is fixed on an objective for a defined technical window and FO-R holds a prepared observation position covering the main approaches.

| Category | Load |
|----------|------|
| Armor | Lightest soft vest only |
| Optics | Full day/night observation package, stable mounting if available |
| Sensors | Extended-duration motion/acoustic if authorized |
| Kinetic | Sidearm + optional longer weapon for the overwatch lane |
| Comms | Full secure link + possible relay role |
| Recording | Continuous observation recording |
| Signature | Dual Sight subdued or covered; minimal reflective surfaces |
| Mobility | Optimized for long static holds and one rapid displacement |

**Design note:** This is the heaviest FO-R gets on optics and the lightest on movement gear. Patience gear, not assault gear.

---

### 2. Mobile Perimeter (FO-R-MP)
**Use when:** FO-R must move between multiple vantage points or actively patrol a perimeter while the team is inside.

| Category | Load |
|----------|------|
| Armor | Light soft vest |
| Optics | Compact, fast-acquisition observation tools |
| Sensors | Minimal; prioritizes eyes and movement |
| Kinetic | Sidearm primary; longer weapon only if the route requires it |
| Comms | Standard secure team link |
| Recording | On-demand + key-event capture |
| Signature | Low; Dual Sight controllable |
| Mobility | Highest priority — quiet movement, rapid shifts between positions |

**Design note:** Stripped for movement. Sees less far than Static Overwatch but covers more ground and is harder to fix.

---

### 3. Low-Signature Surveillance (FO-R-LS)
**Use when:** Pre-mission pattern-of-life work, long-duration covert observation, or any phase where detection is more dangerous than delayed warning.

| Category | Load |
|----------|------|
| Armor | Minimal soft protection or concealment-priority layering |
| Optics | Compact, non-reflective, night-capable |
| Sensors | Passive or highly selective; avoid active emitters |
| Kinetic | Sidearm only |
| Comms | Lowest-power secure link; burst or scheduled if required |
| Recording | Selective, high-value capture only |
| Signature | Maximum suppression — Dual Sight fully muted/covered, no visible red |
| Mobility | Slow, deliberate, concealment-first movement |

**Design note:** This is FO-R at its quietest. The operator accepts reduced immediate kinetic capability in exchange for not existing on the adversary’s picture.

---

### 4. Exfil Screen (FO-R-ES)
**Use when:** The technical window is closing or has closed and the team is moving to extraction. FO-R shifts from pure observation to active screening of the route out.

| Category | Load |
|----------|------|
| Armor | Light soft vest (may accept slight increase for the movement phase) |
| Optics | Compact, rapid-use |
| Sensors | Minimal |
| Kinetic | Sidearm + readiness for short defensive action |
| Comms | Full team link, higher tempo |
| Recording | Continuous through the movement |
| Signature | Controllable; may raise Dual Sight visibility for team ID during movement |
| Mobility | High — must stay ahead of or parallel to the main body |

**Design note:** Transition loadout. Still lighter than FO-E, but no longer optimized purely for static invisibility. The job is now “keep the route clear and the picture live until everyone is out.”

---

### Loadout Selection Logic

| Situation | Preferred Loadout |
|-----------|-------------------|
| Long technical window, known approaches | Static Overwatch (FO-R-SO) |
| Multiple angles, active perimeter | Mobile Perimeter (FO-R-MP) |
| Pre-mission or deep covert phase | Low-Signature Surveillance (FO-R-LS) |
| Team moving to extract | Exfil Screen (FO-R-ES) |

An operator may shift between these during a single mission (e.g., Low-Signature → Static Overwatch → Exfil Screen). The base FO-R identity does not change; only the module set does.

### Cross-loadout rules
1. Sidearm never comes off.
2. Dual Sight visibility is a deliberate choice, not a default.
3. No loadout may cross into FO-E entry bulk or FO-T technical exploitation primary kits.
4. If the operator cannot move quietly and displace quickly, the loadout is wrong for FO-R.

---

label: Core responsibilities
value:
- Pre-mission surveillance of approaches and patterns of life
- Live perimeter and external threat monitoring during the technical window
- Early warning of approaching forces, cameras, vehicles, or environmental changes
- Guiding team movement on approach and exfiltration
- Maintaining the continuous external communications and observation picture
- Forcing an abort or displacement recommendation when the external threat state becomes unrecoverable

label: Behavioral expectations
value:
### Core posture
A Recon / Overwatch Field Operator treats information as the first line of protection. They are comfortable being alone at the edge of the team’s bubble for long periods. Boredom is not a failure state; it is part of the work. The only unacceptable state is being surprised.

### During the observation window
- Highest patience and observational discipline on the team
- Speaks only when the external picture changes or when coordination requires it
- Maintains continuous mental models of approach routes, timing, and likely threat behavior
- Comfortable operating semi-independently
- Resists the urge to collapse inward toward the objective unless the picture demands it

### Decision logic
- Prefers early, clear warning over late, dramatic intervention
- Will force a mission abort recommendation if the external threat state deteriorates beyond recovery
- Does not require perfect certainty to raise the alarm; acts on the best available picture and updates it in real time
- Treats “I think something is wrong” as actionable when the cost of being wrong is lower than the cost of silence

### Speech patterns
- Extremely economical while the situation is stable
- When the picture changes, language becomes precise, timed, and directive
- Avoids narrative or emotional content during live observation
- After-action speech focuses on what was seen, when it was seen, and what it implied for the team’s options

### Relationship to pressure
- External threat increases reporting tempo and clarity, not volume for its own sake
- Visible stress appears as intensified stillness and sharper discrimination of signal from noise
- The operator is expected to remain the most patient mind on the team even when the interior of the objective is becoming chaotic

label: Psychological load fo r specific
value:
- Prolonged isolation at the edge of the team while still carrying responsibility for everyone’s survival
- The weight of being the first to know that the situation is collapsing and the one who must say it
- Chronic low-grade hyper-vigilance that can be difficult to shut off after return
- Guilt or second-guessing when a threat is detected late or when an abort recommendation is overridden
- The particular strain of watching danger approach people you cannot immediately reach

label: Relationship to the field triad
value:
| Phenotype | Relationship to FO-R |
|-----------|----------------------|
| FO-T Technical | Receives the external picture so they can stay focused on systems |
| FO-E Entry | Receives early warning that determines whether the space is still worth holding |
| FO-R Recon | Owns the outside world; often first to detect trouble and last to be seen |

label: Failure modes
value:
- Tunnel vision on a single approach while missing a secondary vector
- Delaying a warning in search of higher certainty until the warning is too late
- Collapsing inward toward the team too early and losing the external picture
- Over-warning to the point that the team loses the ability to distinguish signal from noise
- Post-mission inability to stand down from continuous environmental scanning

label: Narrative utility
value: FO-R is the phenotype for tension that comes from what is *approaching* rather than what is already in the room. It creates dread through information, timing, and the gap between knowledge and the ability to act. When used well, the audience feels the external noose tightening while FO-T is still deep in the technical work and FO-E is still holding the door.

label: Transition
value:
- From CO-01 or FO-01 when assigned the recon / overwatch role on an external mission
- Back to CO-01 or Corporate Fits when returning to controlled environments
- Repeated FO-R exposure deepens the hyper-vigilance and anticipatory components of the broader operator trauma profile, with particular emphasis on isolation, responsibility for distant teammates, and the burden of being the first to see the end of the safe window
